 118 │ class Tag:
 119 │     """
 120 │     A representation of the tag triple for a wheel.
 121 │ 
 122 │     Instances are considered immutable and thus are hashable. Equality checking
 123 │     is also supported.
 124 │ 
 125 │     Instances are safe to serialize with :mod:`pickle`. They use a stable
 126 │     format so the same pickle can be loaded in future packaging releases.
 127 │ 
 128 │     .. versionchanged:: 26.2
 129 │ 
 130 │         Added a stable pickle format. Pickles created with packaging 26.2+ can
 131 │         be unpickled with future releases.  Backward compatibility with pickles
 132 │         from packaging < 26.2 is supported but may be removed in a future
 133 │         release.
 134 │     """
 135 │ 
 136 │     __slots__ = ["_abi", "_hash", "_interpreter", "_platform"]
 137 │ 
 138 │     def __init__(self, interpreter: str, abi: str, platform: str) -> None:
 139 │         """
 140 │         :param str interpreter: The interpreter name, e.g. ``"py"``
 141 │                                 (see :attr:`INTERPRETER_SHORT_NAMES` for mapping
 142 │                                 well-known interpreter names to their short names).
 143 │         :param str abi: The ABI that a wheel supports, e.g. ``"cp37m"``.
 144 │         :param str platform: The OS/platform the wheel supports,
 145 │                             e.g. ``"win_amd64"``.
 146 │         """
 147 │         self._interpreter = interpreter.lower()
 148 │         self._abi = abi.lower()
 149 │         self._platform = platform.lower()
 150 │         # The __hash__ of every single element in a Set[Tag] will be evaluated each time
 151 │         # that a set calls its `.disjoint()` method, which may be called hundreds of
 152 │         # times when scanning a page of links for packages with tags matching that
 153 │         # Set[Tag]. Pre-computing the value here produces significant speedups for
 154 │         # downstream consumers.
 155 │         self._hash = hash((self._interpreter, self._abi, self._platform))

 159 │         """

 161 │         :attr:`INTERPRETER_SHORT_NAMES` for mapping well-known interpreter
 162 │         names to their short names).
 163 │         """

 168 │         """

 170 │         """
 171 │         return self._abi

 186 │             and (self._platform == other._platform)

 233 │ def parse_tag(
 234 │     tag: str, *, validate_order: bool = False, limit: int | None = None
 235 │ ) -> frozenset[Tag]:
 236 │     """
 237 │     Parses the provided tag (e.g. `py3-none-any`) into a frozenset of
 238 │     :class:`Tag` instances.
 239 │ 
 240 │     Returning a set is required due to the possibility that the tag is a
 241 │     `compressed tag set`_, e.g. ``"py2.py3-none-any"`` which supports both
 242 │     Python 2 and Python 3.
 243 │ 
 244 │     If **validate_order** is true, compressed tag set components are checked
 245 │     to be in sorted order as required by PEP 425.
 246 │ 
 247 │     If **limit** is not ``None``, the compressed tag set can generate at most
 248 │     that many tags.
 249 │ 
 250 │     :param str tag: The tag to parse, e.g. ``"py3-none-any"``.
 251 │     :param bool validate_order: Check whether compressed tag set components
 252 │         are in sorted order.
 253 │     :param int | None limit: The maximum number of tags to parse.
 254 │     :raises UnsortedTagsError: If **validate_order** is true and any compressed tag
 255 │         set component is not in sorted order.
 256 │     :raises InvalidTag: If the interpreter field is not an identifier; if the
 257 │         interpreter, ABI, or platform field (or any member of a compressed tag
 258 │         set) is empty; or if the tag does not have exactly three components.
 259 │     :raises TooManyTagsError: If **limit** is not ``None`` and the compressed tag
 260 │         set would generate more than **limit** tags.
 261 │     :raises ValueError: If **limit** is negative.
 262 │ 
 263 │     .. versionadded:: 26.1
 264 │        The *validate_order* parameter.
 265 │ 
 266 │     .. versionadded:: 26.3
 267 │        Raises :class:`InvalidTag` when an interpreter component is not an
 268 │        identifier, a tag component is empty, or a tag does not have exactly
 269 │        three components.
 270 │        Added the *limit* parameter. Raises :class:`TooManyTagsError` if the compressed
 271 │        tag set would generate more than *limit* tags.
 272 │     """
 273 │ 
 274 │     if limit is not None and limit < 0:
 275 │         raise ValueError("limit must be non-negative")
 276 │ 
 277 │     component_parts = [component.split(".") for component in tag.split("-")]
 278 │     for parts in component_parts:
 279 │         if "" in parts:
 280 │             component = ".".join(parts)
 281 │             raise InvalidTag(f"Tag {tag!r} has an empty component: {component!r}")
 282 │         if validate_order and parts != sorted(parts):
 283 │             component = ".".join(parts)
 284 │             raise UnsortedTagsError(
 285 │                 f"Tag component {component!r} is not in sorted order per PEP 425"
 286 │             )
 287 │ 
 288 │     tag_count = 1
 289 │     for parts in component_parts:
 290 │         tag_count *= len(parts)
 291 │ 
 292 │     if limit is not None and tag_count > limit:
 293 │         raise TooManyTagsError(
 294 │             f"Compressed tag set would generate {tag_count} tags, exceeding "
 295 │             f"limit {limit}"
 296 │         )
 297 │ 
 298 │     try:
 299 │         interpreters, abis, platforms = component_parts
 300 │     except ValueError as exc:
 301 │         raise InvalidTag(f"Tag {tag!r} must have exactly three components") from exc
 302 │     for interpreter in interpreters:
 303 │         if not interpreter.isidentifier():
 304 │             raise InvalidTag(f"Tag {tag!r} has an invalid interpreter: {interpreter!r}")
 305 │     return frozenset(
 306 │         Tag(interpreter, abi, platform_)
 307 │         for interpreter in interpreters
 308 │         for abi in abis
 309 │         for platform_ in platforms
 310 │     )

 326 │ def _is_threaded_cpython(abis: list[str]) -> bool:
 327 │     """
 328 │     Determine if the ABI corresponds to a threaded (`--disable-gil`) build.
 329 │ 
 330 │     The threaded builds are indicated by a "t" in the abiflags.
 331 │     """

 365 │ def _cpython_abis(py_version: PythonVersion, warn: bool = False) -> list[str]:
 366 │     py_version = tuple(py_version)  # To allow for version comparison.
 367 │     abis = []
 368 │     version = _version_nodot(py_version[:2])
 369 │     threading = debug = pymalloc = ucs4 = ""
 370 │     with_debug = _get_config_var("Py_DEBUG", warn)
 371 │     has_refcount = hasattr(sys, "gettotalrefcount")
 372 │     # Windows doesn't set Py_DEBUG, so checking for support of debug-compiled
 373 │     # extension modules is the best option.
 374 │     # https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/3383#issuecomment-173267692
 375 │     has_ext = "_d.pyd" in EXTENSION_SUFFIXES
 376 │     if with_debug or (with_debug is None and (has_refcount or has_ext)):
 377 │         debug = "d"
 378 │     if py_version >= (3, 13) and _get_config_var("Py_GIL_DISABLED", warn):
 379 │         threading = "t"
 380 │     if py_version < (3, 8):
 381 │         with_pymalloc = _get_config_var("WITH_PYMALLOC", warn)
 382 │         if with_pymalloc or with_pymalloc is None:
 383 │             pymalloc = "m"
 384 │         if py_version < (3, 3):
 385 │             unicode_size = _get_config_var("Py_UNICODE_SIZE", warn)
 386 │             if unicode_size == 4 or (
 387 │                 unicode_size is None and sys.maxunicode == 0x10FFFF
 388 │             ):
 389 │                 ucs4 = "u"
 390 │     elif debug:
 391 │         # Debug builds can also load "normal" extension modules.
 392 │         # We can also assume no UCS-4 or pymalloc requirement.
 393 │         abis.append(f"cp{version}{threading}")
 394 │     abis.insert(0, f"cp{version}{threading}{debug}{pymalloc}{ucs4}")
 395 │     return abis

 398 │ def cpython_tags(
 399 │     python_version: PythonVersion | None = None,
 400 │     abis: Iterable[str] | None = None,
 401 │     platforms: Iterable[str] | None = None,
 402 │     *,
 403 │     warn: bool = False,
 404 │ ) -> Iterator[Tag]:
 405 │     """
 406 │     Yields the tags for the CPython interpreter.
 407 │ 
 408 │     The specific tags generated are:
 409 │ 
 410 │     - ``cp<python_version>-<abi>-<platform>``
 411 │     - ``cp<python_version>-<stable_abi>-<platform>``
 412 │     - ``cp<python_version>-none-<platform>``
 413 │     - ``cp<older version>-<stable_abi>-<platform>`` where "older version" is all older
 414 │       minor versions down to Python 3.2 (when ``abi3`` was introduced)
 415 │ 
 416 │     If ``python_version`` only provides a major-only version then only
 417 │     user-provided ABIs via ``abis`` and the ``none`` ABI will be used.
 418 │ 
 419 │     The ``stable_abi`` will be either ``abi3`` or ``abi3t`` if `abi` is a
 420 │     GIL-enabled ABI like `"cp315"` or a free-threaded ABI like `"cp315t"`,
 421 │     respectively.
 422 │ 
 423 │     :param Sequence python_version: A one- or two-item sequence representing the
 424 │                                  targeted Python version. Defaults to
 425 │                                  ``sys.version_info[:2]``.
 426 │     :param Iterable abis: Iterable of compatible ABIs. Defaults to the ABIs
 427 │                           compatible with the current system.
 428 │     :param Iterable platforms: Iterable of compatible platforms. Defaults to the
 429 │                                platforms compatible with the current system.
 430 │     :param bool warn: Whether warnings should be logged. Defaults to ``False``.
 431 │ 
 432 │     .. versionadded:: 20.0
 433 │     """
 434 │     if not python_version:
 435 │         python_version = sys.version_info[:2]
 436 │ 
 437 │     interpreter = f"cp{_version_nodot(python_version[:2])}"
 438 │ 
 439 │     if abis is None:
 440 │         abis = _cpython_abis(python_version, warn) if len(python_version) > 1 else []
 441 │     abis = list(abis)
 442 │     threading = _is_threaded_cpython(abis)
 443 │     # Stable ABIs and 'none' are explicitly handled later.
 444 │     explicit_abis = ("abi3", "abi3t", "none") if threading else ("abi3", "none")
 445 │     for explicit_abi in explicit_abis:
 446 │         try:
 447 │             abis.remove(explicit_abi)
 448 │         except ValueError:  # noqa: PERF203
 449 │             pass
 450 │ 
 451 │     platforms = list(platform_tags() if platforms is None else platforms)
 452 │     for abi in abis:
 453 │         for platform_ in platforms:
 454 │             yield Tag(interpreter, abi, platform_)
 455 │ 
 456 │     use_abi3 = _abi3_applies(python_version, threading)
 457 │     use_abi3t = _abi3t_applies(python_version, threading)
 458 │     if use_abi3:
 459 │         yield from (Tag(interpreter, "abi3", platform_) for platform_ in platforms)
 460 │     if use_abi3t:
 461 │         yield from (Tag(interpreter, "abi3t", platform_) for platform_ in platforms)
 462 │ 
 463 │     yield from (Tag(interpreter, "none", platform_) for platform_ in platforms)
 464 │ 
 465 │     if use_abi3 or use_abi3t:
 466 │         for minor_version in range(python_version[1] - 1, 1, -1):
 467 │             for platform_ in platforms:
 468 │                 version = _version_nodot((python_version[0], minor_version))
 469 │                 interpreter = f"cp{version}"
 470 │                 if use_abi3:
 471 │                     yield Tag(interpreter, "abi3", platform_)
 472 │                 if use_abi3t:
 473 │                     # Support for abi3t was introduced in Python 3.15, but in
 474 │                     # principle abi3t wheels are possible for older limited API
 475 │                     # versions, so allow things like ("cp37", "abi3t", "platform")
 476 │                     yield Tag(interpreter, "abi3t", platform_)

 479 │ def _generic_abi() -> list[str]:
 480 │     """
 481 │     Return the ABI tag based on EXT_SUFFIX.
 482 │     """
 483 │     # The following are examples of `EXT_SUFFIX`.
 484 │     # We want to keep the parts which are related to the ABI and remove the
 485 │     # parts which are related to the platform:
 486 │     # - linux:   '.cpython-310-x86_64-linux-gnu.so' => cp310
 487 │     # - mac:     '.cpython-310-darwin.so'           => cp310
 488 │     # - win:     '.cp310-win_amd64.pyd'             => cp310
 489 │     # - win:     '.pyd'                             => cp37 (uses _cpython_abis())
 490 │     # - pypy:    '.pypy38-pp73-x86_64-linux-gnu.so' => pypy38_pp73
 491 │     # - graalpy: '.graalpy-38-native-x86_64-darwin.dylib'
 492 │     #                                               => graalpy_38_native
 493 │ 
 494 │     ext_suffix = _get_config_var("EXT_SUFFIX", warn=True)
 495 │     if not isinstance(ext_suffix, str) or not ext_suffix.startswith("."):
 496 │         raise SystemError("invalid sysconfig.get_config_var('EXT_SUFFIX')")
 497 │     parts = ext_suffix.split(".")
 498 │     if len(parts) < 3:
 499 │         # CPython3.7 and earlier uses ".pyd" on Windows.
 500 │         return _cpython_abis(sys.version_info[:2])
 501 │     soabi = parts[1]
 502 │     if soabi.startswith("cpython"):
 503 │         # non-windows
 504 │         cpython_parts = soabi.split("-")
 505 │         if len(cpython_parts) < 2 or not cpython_parts[1]:
 506 │             raise SystemError("invalid sysconfig.get_config_var('EXT_SUFFIX')")
 507 │         abi = "cp" + cpython_parts[1]
 508 │     elif soabi.startswith("cp"):
 509 │         # windows
 510 │         abi = soabi.split("-")[0]
 511 │     elif soabi.startswith("pypy"):
 512 │         abi = "-".join(soabi.split("-")[:2])
 513 │     elif soabi.startswith("graalpy"):
 514 │         abi = "-".join(soabi.split("-")[:3])
 515 │     elif soabi:
 516 │         # pyston, ironpython, others?
 517 │         abi = soabi
 518 │     else:
 519 │         return []
 520 │     return [_normalize_string(abi)]

 581 │ def pure_python_tags(
 582 │     python_version: PythonVersion | None = None,
 583 │ ) -> Iterator[Tag]:
 584 │     """
 585 │     Yields the pure-Python tags compatible with ``python_version``.
 586 │ 
 587 │     The tags use the ``"none"`` ABI and ``"any"`` platform, so their
 588 │     generation does not depend on the running platform.
 589 │ 
 590 │     .. versionadded:: 26.3
 591 │ 
 592 │     :param Sequence python_version: A one- or two-item sequence representing the
 593 │                                  compatible version of Python. Defaults to
 594 │                                  ``sys.version_info[:2]``.
 595 │     :raises ValueError: If ``python_version`` is an empty sequence.
 596 │     """
 597 │     if python_version is None:

 143 │         :param str abi: The ABI that a wheel supports, e.g. ``"cp37m"``.
 144 │         :param str platform: The OS/platform the wheel supports,
 145 │                             e.g. ``"win_amd64"``.
 146 │         """
 147 │         self._interpreter = interpreter.lower()
 148 │         self._abi = abi.lower()
 149 │         self._platform = platform.lower()
 150 │         # The __hash__ of every single element in a Set[Tag] will be evaluated each time
 151 │         # that a set calls its `.disjoint()` method, which may be called hundreds of
 152 │         # times when scanning a page of links for packages with tags matching that
 153 │         # Set[Tag]. Pre-computing the value here produces significant speedups for
 154 │         # downstream consumers.
 155 │         self._hash = hash((self._interpreter, self._abi, self._platform))
 156 │ 
 157 │     @property
 158 │     def interpreter(self) -> str:
 159 │         """
 160 │         The interpreter name, e.g. ``"py"`` (see
 161 │         :attr:`INTERPRETER_SHORT_NAMES` for mapping well-known interpreter
 162 │         names to their short names).
 163 │         """
 164 │         return self._interpreter
 165 │ 
 166 │     @property
 167 │     def abi(self) -> str:
 168 │         """
 169 │         The supported ABI.
 170 │         """
 171 │         return self._abi
 172 │ 
 173 │     @property
 174 │     def platform(self) -> str:
 175 │         """
 176 │         The OS/platform.
 177 │         """
 178 │         return self._platform
 179 │ 
 180 │     def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
 181 │         if not isinstance(other, Tag):
 182 │             return NotImplemented
 183 │ 
 184 │         return (
 185 │             (self._hash == other._hash)  # Short-circuit ASAP for perf reasons.
 186 │             and (self._platform == other._platform)
 187 │             and (self._abi == other._abi)
 188 │             and (self._interpreter == other._interpreter)
 189 │         )
 190 │ 
 191 │     def __hash__(self) -> int:
 192 │         return self._hash
 193 │ 
 194 │     def __str__(self) -> str:
 195 │         return f"{self._interpreter}-{self._abi}-{self._platform}"
 196 │ 
 197 │     def __repr__(self) -> str:
 198 │         return f"<{self} @ {id(self)}>"
 199 │ 
 200 │     def __getstate__(self) -> tuple[str, str, str]:
 201 │         # Return state as a 3-item tuple: (interpreter, abi, platform).
 202 │         # Cache member _hash is excluded and will be recomputed.
 203 │         return (self._interpreter, self._abi, self._platform)
 204 │ 
 205 │     def __setstate__(self, state: object) -> None:
 206 │         if isinstance(state, tuple):
 207 │             if len(state) == 3 and all(isinstance(s, str) for s in state):
 208 │                 # New format (26.2+): (interpreter, abi, platform)
 209 │                 self._interpreter, self._abi, self._platform = state
 210 │                 self._hash = hash((self._interpreter, self._abi, self._platform))
 211 │                 return
 212 │             if len(state) == 2 and isinstance(state[1], dict):
 213 │                 # Old format (packaging <= 26.1, __slots__): (None, {slot: value}).
 214 │                 _, slots = state
 215 │                 try:
 216 │                     interpreter = slots["_interpreter"]
 217 │                     abi = slots["_abi"]
 218 │                     platform = slots["_platform"]
 219 │                 except KeyError:
 220 │                     raise TypeError(f"Cannot restore Tag from {state!r}") from None
 221 │                 if not all(
 222 │                     isinstance(value, str) for value in (interpreter, abi, platform)
 223 │                 ):
 224 │                     raise TypeError(f"Cannot restore Tag from {state!r}")
 225 │                 self._interpreter = interpreter.lower()
 226 │                 self._abi = abi.lower()
 227 │                 self._platform = platform.lower()
 228 │                 self._hash = hash((self._interpreter, self._abi, self._platform))
 229 │                 return
 230 │         raise TypeError(f"Cannot restore Tag from {state!r}")

 233 │ def parse_tag(
 234 │     tag: str, *, validate_order: bool = False, limit: int | None = None
 235 │ ) -> frozenset[Tag]:
 236 │     """
 237 │     Parses the provided tag (e.g. `py3-none-any`) into a frozenset of
 238 │     :class:`Tag` instances.
 239 │ 
 240 │     Returning a set is required due to the possibility that the tag is a
 241 │     `compressed tag set`_, e.g. ``"py2.py3-none-any"`` which supports both
 242 │     Python 2 and Python 3.
 243 │ 
 244 │     If **validate_order** is true, compressed tag set components are checked
 245 │     to be in sorted order as required by PEP 425.
 246 │ 
 247 │     If **limit** is not ``None``, the compressed tag set can generate at most
 248 │     that many tags.
 249 │ 
 250 │     :param str tag: The tag to parse, e.g. ``"py3-none-any"``.
 251 │     :param bool validate_order: Check whether compressed tag set components
 252 │         are in sorted order.
 253 │     :param int | None limit: The maximum number of tags to parse.
 254 │     :raises UnsortedTagsError: If **validate_order** is true and any compressed tag
 255 │         set component is not in sorted order.
 256 │     :raises InvalidTag: If the interpreter field is not an identifier; if the
 257 │         interpreter, ABI, or platform field (or any member of a compressed tag
 258 │         set) is empty; or if the tag does not have exactly three components.
 259 │     :raises TooManyTagsError: If **limit** is not ``None`` and the compressed tag
 260 │         set would generate more than **limit** tags.
 261 │     :raises ValueError: If **limit** is negative.
 262 │ 
 263 │     .. versionadded:: 26.1
 264 │        The *validate_order* parameter.
 265 │ 
 266 │     .. versionadded:: 26.3
 267 │        Raises :class:`InvalidTag` when an interpreter component is not an
 268 │        identifier, a tag component is empty, or a tag does not have exactly
 269 │        three components.
 270 │        Added the *limit* parameter. Raises :class:`TooManyTagsError` if the compressed
 271 │        tag set would generate more than *limit* tags.
 272 │     """
 273 │ 
 274 │     if limit is not None and limit < 0:
 275 │         raise ValueError("limit must be non-negative")
 276 │ 
 277 │     component_parts = [component.split(".") for component in tag.split("-")]
 278 │     for parts in component_parts:
 279 │         if "" in parts:
 280 │             component = ".".join(parts)
 281 │             raise InvalidTag(f"Tag {tag!r} has an empty component: {component!r}")
 282 │         if validate_order and parts != sorted(parts):
 283 │             component = ".".join(parts)
 284 │             raise UnsortedTagsError(
 285 │                 f"Tag component {component!r} is not in sorted order per PEP 425"
 286 │             )
 287 │ 
 288 │     tag_count = 1
 289 │     for parts in component_parts:
 290 │         tag_count *= len(parts)
 291 │ 
 292 │     if limit is not None and tag_count > limit:
 293 │         raise TooManyTagsError(
 294 │             f"Compressed tag set would generate {tag_count} tags, exceeding "
 295 │             f"limit {limit}"
 296 │         )
 297 │ 
 298 │     try:
 299 │         interpreters, abis, platforms = component_parts
 300 │     except ValueError as exc:
 301 │         raise InvalidTag(f"Tag {tag!r} must have exactly three components") from exc
 302 │     for interpreter in interpreters:
 303 │         if not interpreter.isidentifier():
 304 │             raise InvalidTag(f"Tag {tag!r} has an invalid interpreter: {interpreter!r}")
 305 │     return frozenset(
 306 │         Tag(interpreter, abi, platform_)
 307 │         for interpreter in interpreters
 308 │         for abi in abis
 309 │         for platform_ in platforms
 310 │     )

 326 │ def _is_threaded_cpython(abis: list[str]) -> bool:
 327 │     """
 328 │     Determine if the ABI corresponds to a threaded (`--disable-gil`) build.
 329 │ 
 330 │     The threaded builds are indicated by a "t" in the abiflags.
 331 │     """
 332 │     if len(abis) == 0:
 333 │         return False
 334 │     # expect e.g., cp313
 335 │     m = re.match(r"cp\d+(.*)", abis[0])
 336 │     if not m:
 337 │         return False
 338 │     abiflags = m.group(1)
 339 │     return "t" in abiflags

 342 │ def _abi3_applies(python_version: PythonVersion, threading: bool) -> bool:

 344 │     Determine if the Python version supports abi3.

 347 │     builds do not support abi3.
 348 │     """
 349 │     return len(python_version) > 1 and tuple(python_version) >= (3, 2) and not threading

 352 │ def _abi3t_applies(python_version: PythonVersion, threading: bool) -> bool:
 353 │     """
 354 │     Determine if the Python version supports abi3t.
 355 │ 
 356 │     PEP 803 was first implemented in Python 3.15 but, per PEP 803, this
 357 │     returns tags going back to Python 3.2 to mirror the abi3
 358 │     implementation and leave open the possibility of abi3t wheels
 359 │     supporting older Python versions.

 365 │ def _cpython_abis(py_version: PythonVersion, warn: bool = False) -> list[str]:
 366 │     py_version = tuple(py_version)  # To allow for version comparison.
 367 │     abis = []
 368 │     version = _version_nodot(py_version[:2])
 369 │     threading = debug = pymalloc = ucs4 = ""
 370 │     with_debug = _get_config_var("Py_DEBUG", warn)
 371 │     has_refcount = hasattr(sys, "gettotalrefcount")
 372 │     # Windows doesn't set Py_DEBUG, so checking for support of debug-compiled
 373 │     # extension modules is the best option.
 374 │     # https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/3383#issuecomment-173267692
 375 │     has_ext = "_d.pyd" in EXTENSION_SUFFIXES
 376 │     if with_debug or (with_debug is None and (has_refcount or has_ext)):
 377 │         debug = "d"
 378 │     if py_version >= (3, 13) and _get_config_var("Py_GIL_DISABLED", warn):
 379 │         threading = "t"
 380 │     if py_version < (3, 8):
 381 │         with_pymalloc = _get_config_var("WITH_PYMALLOC", warn)
 382 │         if with_pymalloc or with_pymalloc is None:
 383 │             pymalloc = "m"
 384 │         if py_version < (3, 3):
 385 │             unicode_size = _get_config_var("Py_UNICODE_SIZE", warn)
 386 │             if unicode_size == 4 or (
 387 │                 unicode_size is None and sys.maxunicode == 0x10FFFF
 388 │             ):
 389 │                 ucs4 = "u"
 390 │     elif debug:
 391 │         # Debug builds can also load "normal" extension modules.
 392 │         # We can also assume no UCS-4 or pymalloc requirement.
 393 │         abis.append(f"cp{version}{threading}")
 394 │     abis.insert(0, f"cp{version}{threading}{debug}{pymalloc}{ucs4}")
 395 │     return abis

 398 │ def cpython_tags(
 399 │     python_version: PythonVersion | None = None,
 400 │     abis: Iterable[str] | None = None,
 401 │     platforms: Iterable[str] | None = None,
 402 │     *,
 403 │     warn: bool = False,
 404 │ ) -> Iterator[Tag]:
 405 │     """
 406 │     Yields the tags for the CPython interpreter.
 407 │ 
 408 │     The specific tags generated are:
 409 │ 
 410 │     - ``cp<python_version>-<abi>-<platform>``
 411 │     - ``cp<python_version>-<stable_abi>-<platform>``
 412 │     - ``cp<python_version>-none-<platform>``
 413 │     - ``cp<older version>-<stable_abi>-<platform>`` where "older version" is all older
 414 │       minor versions down to Python 3.2 (when ``abi3`` was introduced)
 415 │ 
 416 │     If ``python_version`` only provides a major-only version then only
 417 │     user-provided ABIs via ``abis`` and the ``none`` ABI will be used.
 418 │ 
 419 │     The ``stable_abi`` will be either ``abi3`` or ``abi3t`` if `abi` is a
 420 │     GIL-enabled ABI like `"cp315"` or a free-threaded ABI like `"cp315t"`,
 421 │     respectively.
 422 │ 
 423 │     :param Sequence python_version: A one- or two-item sequence representing the
 424 │                                  targeted Python version. Defaults to
 425 │                                  ``sys.version_info[:2]``.
 426 │     :param Iterable abis: Iterable of compatible ABIs. Defaults to the ABIs
 427 │                           compatible with the current system.
 428 │     :param Iterable platforms: Iterable of compatible platforms. Defaults to the
 429 │                                platforms compatible with the current system.
 430 │     :param bool warn: Whether warnings should be logged. Defaults to ``False``.
 431 │ 
 432 │     .. versionadded:: 20.0
 433 │     """
 434 │     if not python_version:
 435 │         python_version = sys.version_info[:2]
 436 │ 
 437 │     interpreter = f"cp{_version_nodot(python_version[:2])}"
 438 │ 
 439 │     if abis is None:
 440 │         abis = _cpython_abis(python_version, warn) if len(python_version) > 1 else []
 441 │     abis = list(abis)
 442 │     threading = _is_threaded_cpython(abis)
 443 │     # Stable ABIs and 'none' are explicitly handled later.
 444 │     explicit_abis = ("abi3", "abi3t", "none") if threading else ("abi3", "none")
 445 │     for explicit_abi in explicit_abis:
 446 │         try:
 447 │             abis.remove(explicit_abi)
 448 │         except ValueError:  # noqa: PERF203
 449 │             pass
 450 │ 
 451 │     platforms = list(platforms or platform_tags())
 452 │     for abi in abis:
 453 │         for platform_ in platforms:
 454 │             yield Tag(interpreter, abi, platform_)
 455 │ 
 456 │     use_abi3 = _abi3_applies(python_version, threading)
 457 │     use_abi3t = _abi3t_applies(python_version, threading)
 458 │     if use_abi3:
 459 │         yield from (Tag(interpreter, "abi3", platform_) for platform_ in platforms)
 460 │     if use_abi3t:
 461 │         yield from (Tag(interpreter, "abi3t", platform_) for platform_ in platforms)
 462 │ 
 463 │     yield from (Tag(interpreter, "none", platform_) for platform_ in platforms)
 464 │ 
 465 │     if use_abi3 or use_abi3t:
 466 │         for minor_version in range(python_version[1] - 1, 1, -1):
 467 │             for platform_ in platforms:
 468 │                 version = _version_nodot((python_version[0], minor_version))
 469 │                 interpreter = f"cp{version}"
 470 │                 if use_abi3:
 471 │                     yield Tag(interpreter, "abi3", platform_)
 472 │                 if use_abi3t:
 473 │                     # Support for abi3t was introduced in Python 3.15, but in
 474 │                     # principle abi3t wheels are possible for older limited API
 475 │                     # versions, so allow things like ("cp37", "abi3t", "platform")
 476 │                     yield Tag(interpreter, "abi3t", platform_)
 477 │

 479 │ def _generic_abi() -> list[str]:
 480 │     """
 481 │     Return the ABI tag based on EXT_SUFFIX.
 482 │     """
 483 │     # The following are examples of `EXT_SUFFIX`.
 484 │     # We want to keep the parts which are related to the ABI and remove the
 485 │     # parts which are related to the platform:
 486 │     # - linux:   '.cpython-310-x86_64-linux-gnu.so' => cp310
 487 │     # - mac:     '.cpython-310-darwin.so'           => cp310
 488 │     # - win:     '.cp310-win_amd64.pyd'             => cp310
 489 │     # - win:     '.pyd'                             => cp37 (uses _cpython_abis())
 490 │     # - pypy:    '.pypy38-pp73-x86_64-linux-gnu.so' => pypy38_pp73
 491 │     # - graalpy: '.graalpy-38-native-x86_64-darwin.dylib'
 492 │     #                                               => graalpy_38_native
 493 │ 
 494 │     ext_suffix = _get_config_var("EXT_SUFFIX", warn=True)
 495 │     if not isinstance(ext_suffix, str) or not ext_suffix.startswith("."):
 496 │         raise SystemError("invalid sysconfig.get_config_var('EXT_SUFFIX')")
 497 │     parts = ext_suffix.split(".")
 498 │     if len(parts) < 3:
 499 │         # CPython3.7 and earlier uses ".pyd" on Windows.
 500 │         return _cpython_abis(sys.version_info[:2])
 501 │     soabi = parts[1]
 502 │     if soabi.startswith("cpython"):
 503 │         # non-windows
 504 │         cpython_parts = soabi.split("-")
 505 │         if len(cpython_parts) < 2 or not cpython_parts[1]:
 506 │             raise SystemError("invalid sysconfig.get_config_var('EXT_SUFFIX')")
 507 │         abi = "cp" + cpython_parts[1]
 508 │     elif soabi.startswith("cp"):
 509 │         # windows
 510 │         abi = soabi.split("-")[0]
 511 │     elif soabi.startswith("pypy"):
 512 │         abi = "-".join(soabi.split("-")[:2])
 513 │     elif soabi.startswith("graalpy"):
 514 │         abi = "-".join(soabi.split("-")[:3])
 515 │     elif soabi:
 516 │         # pyston, ironpython, others?
 517 │         abi = soabi
 518 │     else:
 519 │         return []
 520 │     return [_normalize_string(abi)]
